decisions: _plan_key and _plan_type move to purchase_plans.py, two defs past the map's list. purchase_plans reads _plan_key and purchase_search reads _plan_type, and the map left both in the optimize_build remainder, which is a back-edge from two modules. A purchase plan's identity and its type are the plan space's own vocabulary, so purchase_plans.py is the reader-named home.

Measured residue: 516 lines, sixteen over the ceiling, so optimize_build's size finding does not clear on this assignment alone. The cut the map says the plan must name: optimize_build's locked-item and pool resolution, from 'Resolve locked items' to the boots_pool assignment (currently lines 1877 to 1929, 53 lines), becomes a top-level _resolve_locked_fill that returns the resolved locked items, their names, the resolved locked boots, the boots_locked flag, slots_to_fill, fill_boots, pool and boots_pool. Its home is optimizer_candidates.py, whose name already promises 'which items a search may legally hold': add the def name there and re-run this assignment once the cut lands, taking the residue to about 463 and optimizer_candidates to about 160.

Not the runner-up sweep. It is the other candidate cut the map names, but it closes over remember_candidate and mutates total_evals, so extracting it means a twelve-parameter signature and a two-value return, against a locked-item block that is pure resolution with no closure capture.

The two local-search drivers go to purchase_plans.py, not to purchase_search.py as the map has them. Measured both ways: with them, purchase_search.py renders at 505 lines and reopens the finding it was extracted to close; without, purchase_plans lands at 482 and purchase_search at 433. _score_exhaustive_purchase_plans and _run_purchase_local_search are searches over the plan space rather than the public entry point, so the concept follows the measurement.

Published spelling, for every name a sibling now reads: build_evaluation's evaluate_build and build_timeline_coverage, build_receipts' public_search_timeline_coverage, and purchase_plans' PurchaseSearch, plan_type, run_purchase_local_search, score_exhaustive_purchase_plans and enumerate_affordable_shapes.
